conditions.text: What the saṃjñā names: 'vibhāṣā' is a name for the two MEANINGS 'not' (pratiṣedha) and 'optionally' (vikalpa); the इति makes the meanings, not the words न/वा, the saṃjñin. So 1.1.44 itself is a definition — it applies wherever a rule is a vibhāṣā, not inside 1.1.44.

quotes.quote: नेति प्रतिषेधो वेति विकल्पः, तयोः प्रतिषेधविकल्पयोर्विभाषेति संज्ञा भवति। इतिकरणोऽर्थनिर्देशार्थः।
नवेति यावर्थौ प्रतीयेते प्रतिषेधविकल्पौ, तयोरेवेयं संज्ञा भवति; न नवाशब्द-योः।

conditions.text: How it operates: in a vibhāṣā rule both 'not' and 'optionally' are present; the 'not' first levels the domain, then the option operates. The tradition (Kāśikā, TB) says the saṃjñā is needed only for ubhayatra-vibhāṣā (both prāpta and aprāpta sub-domains); in a pure prāpta- or aprāpta-vibhāṣā the word's ordinary sense already suffices. The Bhāṣya classifies vibhāṣā rules as prāpte / aprāpte / ubhayatra.

quotes.quote: विभाषाप्रदेशेषु प्रतिषेधविकल्पावुपतिष्ठेते। तत्र प्रतिषेधेन समीकृते विषये पश्चाद् विकल्पः प्रवर्तते। उभयत्रविभाषाः प्रयोजयन्ति।
उभयत्रविभाषार्थं चेदं सूत्रम् । प्राप्तविभाषायामप्राप्तविभाषायां च नास्योपयोगः ।

conditions.text: Scope beyond the word विभाषा (view-dependent — the basis on which वा / अन्यतरस्याम् credits are accepted here): the Bhāṣya itself treats अन्यतरस्याम्- and वा-sūtras (हृक्रोरन्यतरस्याम्, अनुपसर्गाद्वा, उषविदजागृभ्योऽन्यतरस्याम्) in its prāpta/aprāpta/ubhayatra survey under 1.1.44 and says Pāṇini mostly conveys this sense with other words (बहुलम्, अन्यतरस्याम्, उभयथा, वा, एकेषाम्). Bālamanoramā makes it explicit: विभाषा in the sūtra stands for every option-word; Tattvabodhinī: making the MEANING the saṃjñin is what covers हृक्रोरन्यतरस्याम्.

quotes.quote: आचार्यः खल्वपि सञ्ज्ञामारभमाणो भूयिष्ठमन्यैरपि शब्दैरेतमर्थं सम्प्रत्याययति -  बहुलमन्यतरस्यामुभयथा वा एकेषामिति।
॥ हृक्रोरन्यतरस्याम् । प्राप्ते अप्राप्ते उभयत्र वेति सन्देहः।

conditions.text: Dissent to record (not used to reject credits, since it rejects the sūtra wholesale): Bhāṣya/Nāgeśa hold the option words work as in ordinary usage and the sūtra is rejected (pratyākhyāta); Padamañjarī: on the per-instance view, अन्यतरस्याम् / वा get the right result without the saṃjñā. Nāgeśa rejects TB's 'meaning is the saṃjñā' move.

quotes.quote: भाष्ये तु विभाषादिशब्दानां लोकवद् एव केवलविकल्पपरत्वेऽपि लक्ष्यानुरोधेनैव क्वचिद् विधिमुखेन क्वचिन्निषेधमुखेन विकल्पस्य प्रवृत्युपपत्तेरेतत्सूत्रं प्रत्याख्यातम्
तता च 'हृक्रोरन्यतरस्याम्' इत्यादावन्यतरस्यांग्रहणे वा ग्रहणे चोभयत्रविभाषास्विष्टसिद्धः ।

conditions.text: Ācārya names and बहुलम्: they count as option words only where the commentary says so (Kāśikā: उदीचाम्/प्राचाम्/अन्यतरस्याम्/बहुलम् are all vikalpārtha; the ācārya word may be merely honorific where an option is already carried) — but an ācārya/region word is NOT an option when it only restricts (Kāśikā 2.4.60). बहुलम् is wider than option (always/never/optional/otherwise).

quotes.quote: उदीचां प्राचामन्यतरस्यां बहुलमिति सर्व एते विकल्पार्थास्तेषामेकेनैव सिध्यति। तत्राचार्यग्रहणं पूजार्थम्। बहुलग्रहणं वैचित्र्यार्थम्।
गोत्रविशेषणं प्राग्ग्रहणम् ,न विकल्पार्थम्

conditions.text: Limit: a carried option word licenses the credit only where it is actually in force in that sūtra — the Kāśikā can say a rule is nitya inside a vibhāṣā adhikāra, or a new word (नित्यम्) / a prohibition / an obligatory placement rule overrides it. A vyavasthita-vibhāṣā is still a vibhāṣā.

1.1.46.generalExplanation: a टित् augment goes at the BEGINNING, a कित् one at the END

conditions.text: C1. Content: an augment marked ṭ becomes the first part, one marked k the last part, of what is named in the 6th case. It places an augment (āgama) that a sūtra teaches.

conditions.text: C2. Only augments: a ṭ/k marker on a suffix or on a substitute does not bring in 1.1.46 (a suffix cannot be part of anything; इट् in the tiṅ list is a substitute of ल).

1.1.49.generalExplanation: a word in the 6th case in a rule names WHAT IS REPLACED — so we read “… स्थाने”

conditions.text: C1. Scope: a ṣaṣṭhī uttered in the śāstra (a sūtra word, or one carried by anuvṛtti) whose relation is not otherwise fixed is read as 'in the place of' (sthāna = prasaṅga). Checkable: the word must really be a 6th in function and name a sound/form of the grammar, and the relation must be word-to-word.

quotes.quote: इह शास्त्रे या षष्ठी अनियतयोगा श्रूयते, सा स्थानेयोगैव भवति नान्ययोगा।
स्थानशब्दश्च प्रसङ्गवाची।

conditions.text: C2. It is a niyama: it works only where the relation would be in doubt. If another word — in the sūtra or carried by anuvṛtti — names the part actually replaced (उपधा, एच्, अच्, ह्, अभ्यास, a visarga …), the 6th of the whole is an avayava/viśeṣaṇa-ṣaṣṭhī. Test (Bhāṣya 6.4.1): a 6th that needs a link to another word is a viśeṣaṇa-ṣaṣṭhī. Carried words count: Kāśikā 6.4.35 makes शासः a place-6th only once उपधायाः has stopped. A samānādhikaraṇa qualifier of the sthānin (e.g. अनन्त्ययोः तदोः) shares its relation and is treated here as licensed.

quotes.quote: अवयवषष्ठ्यादीनां च नियमस्याप्राप्तिः। किं कारणम्? योगस्यासंदिग्धत्वात्। सन्देहे नियमः।
शास इदङ् हलोरिति शासेश्चान्त्यस्य स्यादुपधामात्रस्य च। ऊदुपधाया गोहः इति गोहेश्चान्त्यस्य स्यादुपधामात्रस्य च।

conditions.text: C3. There must be a substitute: the relation fixed is sthāni–ādeśa. Where the rule teaches no substitute (saṃjñā, atideśa, prakṛtibhāva, asiddhatva, an affix or gender rule), and for an adhikāra used only to name, 1.1.49 has no work.

quotes.quote: योगः पुनरिह स्थान्यादेशभावलक्षणः।
यत्र ह्रादेशो विधीयते -<<अस्तेर्भूः>> [[2.4.52]]  इत्येवमादौ तत्रास्याः परिभाषाया व्यापारः

conditions.text: C4. Augments: 1.1.46 (ṭit/kit) and 1.1.47 (mit) are apavādas of 1.1.49 — the 6th in an augment rule names the host, not a place to be replaced.

quotes.quote: <<षष्ठी स्थानेयोगा>> [[1.1.49]]  इत्यस्याः परिभाषाया अयमपवादः।
आदिष्टिद् भवति अन्तःकिद् भवति षष्ठीनिर्दिष्टस्य।

conditions.text: C5. Anuvāda (limit, disputed): Nyāsa, Padamañjarī and Bālamanoramā on 7.3.46 say the paribhāṣā works in a vidhi, not in an anuvāda (hence 7.3.46's explicit स्थाने); Śekhara (PIS 102) rejects that jñāpaka and calls the स्थाने merely explanatory. Padamañjarī on 1.1.45 nevertheless gets the place for anuvāda यणः from 1.1.49 as adhikāra.

quotes.quote: आदेशविधौ <<अस्तेर्भूः>> [[2.4.52]]  इत्येवमादौ <<षष्ठी स्थानेयोगा>> [[1.1.49]]  इत्येषा परिभाषोपतिष्ठते, न त्वनुवादे; विधिवाक्यशेषभूतत्वादस्याः।
अनुवादे परिभाषाणामनुपस्थितेः

conditions.text: C6. Only what is actually uttered in the 6th is bound (Śekhara PIS 12, derived from 1.1.49): a place that is only inferred or supplied by commentary is not covered without more.

quotes.quote: षष्ठ्यन्तं निर्दिश्यमानम् = उच्चार्यमाणमुच्चार्यमाणसजातीयमेव, निर्दिश्यमानावयवरूपमेव वा स्थानेन स्थाननिरूपितसम्बन्धेन युज्यते, न तु प्रतीयमानमित्यर्थः।

conditions.text: C7. Doubling: in the 6.1 dvitva section dvirvacana is repeated utterance (no substitution); in the 8.1 and 8.4 sections it is substitution ('सर्वस्य स्थाने द्वे').

quotes.quote: द्विःप्रयोगश्च द्विर्वचनमिदम्, आवृत्तिसंख्या हि द्वे इति विधीयते। तेन स एव शब्दो द्विरुच्चार्यते, न च शब्दान्तरं तस्य स्थाने विधीयते॥
द्विः प्रयोग एवात्र विधीयते, न स्थानषष्ठीमाश्रित्यादेशपक्ष इति प्रकृतसूत्रभाष्ये प्रपञ्चितम्

conditions.text: C8. Tripādī: asiddhatva does not block 1.1.49 for the 6ths of 8.2–8.4 (Kāśikā 8.2.1). The carried पदस्य (8.1.16) is a place-6th where the pada itself is replaced (Nyāsa, e.g. संयोगान्तस्य लोपः) but only a qualifier of the thing operated on elsewhere (Padamañjarī).

quotes.quote: `पदस्य` इत्येषा स्थानषष्ठी।

conditions.text: C9. Samprasāraṇa (open point): Kāśikā glosses X-स्य सम्प्रसारणम् as 'ik in place of yaṇ'; the yaṇ place comes from 1.1.45.

इग्यो यणः स्थाने भूतो भावी वा तस्य संप्रसारणमित्येषा संज्ञा भवति।

conditions.text: C1 — 1.1.50: when a substitute is due, the most similar (sadṛśatama) one comes.

conditions.text: C2 — It works only where one sthānin could get several substitutes; it picks among them. So it needs an actual substitution with more than one candidate — not a prohibition, not a single named substitute.

1.1.51.gloss: an aṇ replacing ऋ/ऌ comes with र्/ल् (अर्, आर्, अल्)
1.1.51.generalExplanation: ऋ replaced by a / i / u comes with र्

conditions.text: C1 — An अण् that comes in place of ऋ (ऋ standing for ऋ/ॠ/ऌ) comes with र् (ल् for ऌ) after it, at the moment it is enjoined.

quotes.quote: उः स्थानेऽण् प्रसज्यमान एव रपरो वेदितव्यः।
तत्स्थाने योऽण् स रपरः सन्नेव प्रवर्तते ।

conditions.text: C2 — The sthānin must be ऋ; elsewhere nothing is added. Kāśikā examples: कर्ता, हर्ता (guṇa), किरति, गिरति (7.1.100), द्वैमातुरः (4.1.115).

quotes.quote: उरिति किम्? खेयम्। गेयम्।
कर्ता। हर्ता। किरति। गिरति। द्वैमातुरः। त्रैमातुरः।

conditions.text: C3 — अण् is the earlier अण् (अ इ उ), so a substitute like र् (yaṇ) or ऋ itself takes nothing.

quotes.quote: वस्तुतस्तु 'उरण्रपरः' इत्यत्राऽजिति वक्तव्ये अण्ग्रहणसामर्थ्दाण्पूर्वेणैवेत्युक्तं भाष्ये ।

1.1.52.gloss: a replacement replaces the LAST sound
1.1.52.generalExplanation: a substitute replaces only the LAST sound

conditions.text: C1 — What 1.1.52 does: a substitute taught for something named in the 6th case (sthāna-ṣaṣṭhī) replaces only the LAST sound (al) of it. Its work is to pick ONE sound out of a longer whole (KV example इद् गोण्याः; BM/TB example त्यदादीनामः → यः, सः).

quotes.quote: षष्ठीनिर्दिष्टस्य य उच्यत आदेशः, सोऽन्त्यस्यालः स्थाने वेदितव्यः।
षष्ठीनिर्दिष्टस्यान्त्यस्याल आदेशः स्यात्

conditions.text: C2 — Only for a sthāna-ṣaṣṭhī and only for substitutes: augments (ṭit/kit/mit) are explicitly outside it (they are placed by 1.1.46/1.1.47).

quotes.quote: इतरथा ह्यनिष्टं प्रसज्येत। टित्किन्मितोऽप्यन्त्यस्य स्युः।
स्थानषष्ठीति किम् ,आर्धधातुकस्यैट् तृच् ऋकारात्पूर्वो मा भूत् ।

conditions.text: C3 — The substitute must be ONE sound. A substitute of several sounds, or a śit, replaces the WHOLE (1.1.55, the apavāda of 1.1.52; it also beats 1.1.54); a ṅit substitute of several sounds goes on the last sound by 1.1.53. it-markers do not count as sounds (नानुबन्धकृतमनेकाल्त्वम्).

quotes.quote: आदेशः पुनरत्रैकाल्लभ्यते।
अनेकाल् य आदेशः शिच् च, स सर्वस्य षष्ठीनिर्दिष्टस्य स्थाने भवति।

conditions.text: C4 — After a 5th-case word the operation is on the FIRST sound of what follows (1.1.54, apavāda of 1.1.52).

quotes.quote: परस्य कार्यं शिष्यमाणमादेरलः प्रत्येतव्यम्
क्व च परस्य कार्यं शिष्यते? यत्र पञ्चमीनिर्देशः।

conditions.text: C5 — If the place is itself named as one sound (a varṇa/pratyāhāra in the 6th, carried or own: विसर्जनीयस्य, निष्ठातकारस्य, एचः, इटः, the य of a suffix …) or by a position word (उपधायाः, आदेः, अनन्त्यस्य, टेः), 1.1.52 decides nothing. The Bhāṣya (quoted by Nāgeśa) says of the visarga case वृक्षस्तत्र that “निर्दिश्यमानस्येत्येव सिद्धम्”; the Kāśikā repeatedly gives a place word the purpose “अलोऽन्त्यस्य मा भूत्”.

quotes.quote: अयोगवहानामुपदेशेऽलोन्त्यविधिः प्रयोजनम् । वृक्षस्तत्र, नैतदस्ति प्रयोजनम्, निर्दिश्यमानस्येत्येव सिद्धम्
उपाधाया इति किम् ? अलोऽन्त्यस्य [[१.१.५२]] मा भूत्।

conditions.text: C6 — Exception “नानर्थकेऽलोऽन्त्यविधिरनभ्यासविकारे” (PIS 105): when the named place is a meaningless piece (ति of विंशति, इद् of इदम्, न of स्तेन) 1.1.52 does not apply and the whole piece goes; abhyāsa changes are excepted from the exception (so 1.1.52 does apply to the abhyāsa).

quotes.quote: नानर्थकेऽलोन्त्यविधिरनभ्यासविकारे
अलोऽन्त्यस्ये॑ति न भवति,नानर्थकेऽलोऽन्त्यविधि॑रित्युक्तेः

conditions.text: C7 — ह्रस्व/दीर्घ/प्लुत (and guṇa/vṛddhi through 1.1.3) on a named whole: 1.2.28 makes the ac the place. When the sound QUALIFIES the whole (अजन्तस्य, इगन्तस्य …: tadanta) the 6th is sthāna-ṣaṣṭhī of the whole and 1.1.52 takes its last sound; when the vowel is medial (शाम्यति, क्रामति, ऊह्), the reading is “the ac of X” and 1.1.52 has no role.

quotes.quote: ह्रस्वदीर्घप्लुताः स्वसंज्ञया शिष्यमाणा अच एव स्थाने वेदितव्याः।

1.1.55.gloss: a multi-sound / śit replacement replaces the whole
1.1.55.generalExplanation: a substitute of more than one sound (or शित्) replaces the WHOLE

conditions.text: C1 — What 1.1.55 says: a substitute (ādeśa) that has more than one sound (anekāl), or that is śit, replaces the WHOLE of the sthānin named in the 6th case. It is the apavāda of 1.1.52 अलोऽन्त्यस्य (single last sound). Scope = a substitution of a 6th-case sthānin; an augment, a new suffix, a nipātana, an atideśa, a prohibition, or a number/gender/case rule is outside it.

quotes.quote: अनेकाल् य आदेशः शिच् च, स सर्वस्य षष्ठीनिर्दिष्टस्य स्थाने भवति।

conditions.text: C2 — "More than one sound" is counted AFTER the anubandhas (it-letters) are removed: नानुबन्धकृतमनेकाल्त्वम्, made known by the separate mention of śit in 1.1.55. So तृ (= त्), उत् (= उ, the त् only marks tapara), अङ् (= अ), सिच् (= स्) are single-sound substitutes and replace only the last sound (1.1.52) unless the sthānin is itself one sound. The sources name 6.4.127 अर्वणस्तृ and 6.1.131 दिव उत् as places with NO sarvādeśa.

शिद्ग्रहणमेवैतज्ज्ञापकम् । तेन <<अर्वणस्तृ>> [[6.4.127]] इत्यादेर्न सर्वादेशत्वम् ।

conditions.text: C3 — Exception to C2 for an INITIAL it-letter that is an it only because the substitute is a pratyaya (चुटू 1.3.7, लशक्वतद्धिते 1.3.8, षः प्रत्ययस्य 1.3.6): when the substitute is enjoined it is not yet a pratyaya, so that letter still counts, the substitute is anekāl and replaces the whole; only then does the letter become an it. Stated for डा (2.4.85) and णल् (3.4.82).

quotes.quote: डादिविषये तु सर्वादेशत्वं विनानुबन्धत्वस्यैवाभावेनानुपूर्व्यात्सिद्धम्

conditions.text: C5 — 1.1.54 आदेः परस्य vs 1.1.55: when the sthānin follows a 5th-case word AND the substitute is anekāl/śit, 1.1.55 wins by paratva — the whole is replaced (अतो भिस ऐस्, अष्टाभ्य औश्).

quotes.quote: अतो भिस ऐस्। अनेकाल्शित्सर्वस्येत्येतद् भवति विप्रतिषेधेन।

conditions.text: C6 — When the sthānin is itself a single sound (e.g. च्लि = ल्, since its इ is for pronunciation and its च् an anubandha; ल् of the lakāras; एच्; णि = इ), any substitute replaces "the whole" trivially. 1.1.55 then decides nothing; its condition may still hold (anekāl substitute) — such credits are counted licensed but redundant.

णल्: a single sound → it replaces the LAST sound
गमिः → the substitute: “गमिः आदेशः” (read from its case) · काशिका: “गमिरादेशो भवति” — also: गमिः: more than one sound → it replaces the WHOLE of the place

तिप् etc.: more than one sound → it replaces the WHOLE of the place

1.1.56.gloss: the replacement is treated like the replaced (sthānivat), except in single-sound rules
1.1.56.generalExplanation: a substitute behaves like the original (except in a rule about single sounds)

conditions.text: C1 — What 1.1.56 is: an atideśa (extension). Because substitute and original are different, operations conditioned by the original would not reach the substitute; 1.1.56 makes the substitute behave like the original for those OPERATIONS (kārya), except operations conditioned by a single sound (al) of the original.

quotes.quote: स्थान्यादेशयोः पृथक्त्वात् स्थान्याश्रयं कार्यमादेशे न प्राप्नोतीत्ययमतिदेश आरभ्यते।
स्थानिवदादेशो भवति स्थान्याश्रयेषु कार्येष्वनलाश्रयेषु, स्थान्यलाश्रयाणि कार्याणि वर्जयित्वा।

conditions.text: C2 — What counts as an ādeśa (and as a sthānin): the ādeśa is what, when enjoined, makes the other (that was due) cease; the sthānin is that in whose place something else is enjoined. An āgama (added element), a pratyaya newly introduced, a nipātana, a prakṛti-bhāva (no change), a vacana/liṅga/vibhakti rule, or an atideśa (-vat) introduces no substitute, so 1.1.56 has nothing to act on there.

quotes.quote: यस्य स्थानेऽन्यद्विधीयते तत्स्थानि । येन विधीयमानेन अन्यत्प्रसक्तं निवर्तते स आदेशः ।

conditions.text: C3 — What is inherited: the status that operations of the śāstra depend on (dhātu-, aṅga-, kṛt-, taddhita-, avyaya-, sup-, tiṅ-, pada-hood …), so that a LATER rule conditioned by that status applies to the substitute. Only śāstric operations are extended.

quotes.quote: किमुदाहरणम्? धात्वङ्गकृत्तद्धिताव्ययसुप्तिङ्पदादेशाः।
आर्धधातुके विषये प्रागेवादेशेषु कृतेषु <<धातोः>> [[३.१.९१]] इति तव्यादयो भवन्ति।

conditions.text: C4 — The anal-vidhi exception: no sthānivad-bhāva for an operation that depends on a sound (al) of the original (द्यौः, पन्थाः, सः).

quotes.quote: अनल्विधाविति किम्? द्युपथित्यदादेशा न स्थानिवद् भवन्ति।
अलाश्रयकार्ये कर्तव्ये स्थानिवन्न भवतीति फलितम् ।

conditions.text: C5 — 1.1.57–1.1.59 extend and limit it for vowel-substitutes (1.1.57: a vowel-substitute caused by what follows is sthānivat even in a rule about what precedes; 1.1.58: not in the listed rules; 1.1.59: for reduplication, before a vowel that conditions it). These three sūtras take आदेशः (and स्थानिवत्) from 1.1.56 by anuvṛtti.

quotes.quote: आदेशः स्थानिवद् इति वर्तते।
अजादेशः परनिमित्तकः पूर्वविधौ कर्तव्ये स्थानिवद् भवति।

conditions.text: C6 — Where commentators invoke it: at the point where a later operation is to be done ('… कर्तव्ये'), i.e. in deriving forms — not in stating the substitution rule itself. In an ādeśa-vidhi the vṛtti is 'Y-sthāne X ādeśo bhavati', which comes from 1.1.49 (6th case = sthāne) and 1.1.50–55 (which part is replaced); 1.1.56 adds nothing to that sentence. At ādeśa-vidhis commentators mention 1.1.56 either (a) in deriving the examples, (b) to explain the purpose of a word of the sūtra that cancels or replaces what sthānivad-bhāva would give (अपित्, ङित्, an anubandha), or (c) to say it does NOT apply. None of these changes the reading of the sūtra into its vṛtti. The reading genuinely depends on 1.1.56 only where its words are carried (1.1.57–59).

quotes.quote: स्थानिवद्भावेन कर्त्रभिप्रायक्रियाफलविवक्षायामात्मनेपदं भवति।

1.1.66.generalExplanation: a word in the 7th case names what must FOLLOW — so we read “… परे”

conditions.text: Core rule: a word in the 7th case that stands for a following element (a para-saptamī, i.e. a sat-/aupaśleṣika-saptamī naming a sound, suffix or word) makes the operation fall on the element BEFORE it, never on the one after it. It is a restricting rule (niyama): the locative alone could point either way.

quotes.quote: तस्मिन्निति सप्तम्यर्थनिर्देशे पूर्वस्यैव कार्यं भवति, नोत्तरस्य।

conditions.text: Immediacy: 'nirdiṣṭa' means the operation falls on the IMMEDIATELY preceding element — no intervening sound (time-gaps outside saṃhitā are not counted). So a 7th that names something which follows a different, intervening element (e.g. परस्मैपदेषु after sic) does not by 1.1.66 make the earlier element the kāryin.

conditions.text: Only a 7th of a WORD-FORM, never of a meaning: a 7th naming a sense, a circumstance or a domain has no before/after relation and is outside 1.1.66.

conditions.text: Immediacy: 'nirdiṣṭa' carries over from 1.1.66, so the operation falls on what comes IMMEDIATELY after (no other sound in between). conditions.text: The element after the 5th-case word must ALREADY BE THERE (sat), and the operation is done to it: substitution, augment, deletion/luk, accent, ṣatva/ṇatva, a kit/ṅit transfer, a saṃjñā, the choice of pada endings for an existing l. Placing a NEW suffix after a base (a suffix-introducing rule) is NOT 1.1.67's domain: the suffix's position comes from 3.1.2 परश्च. The Mahābhāṣya repeats the rule: 'in a suffix-introducing rule, 5th cases do not create a 6th (by 1.1.67)'.

quotes.quote: उभयनिर्देशे विप्रतिषेधात् पञ्चमीनिर्देशः। उभयनिर्देशे विप्रतिषेधात् पञ्चमीनिर्देशो भविष्यति। किं प्रयोजनम् ? प्रयोजनमतो लसार्वधातुकानुदात्तत्वे। वक्ष्यति तास्यादिभ्योऽनुदात्तत्वे सप्तमीनिर्देशोऽभ्यस्तसिजर्थ इति। तस्मिन् क्रियमाणे तास्यादिभ्यः परस्य लसार्वधातुकस्य लसार्वधातुके परतस्तास्यादीनामिति सन्देहः। तास्यादिभ्यः परस्य लसार्वधातुकस्य। बहोरिष्ठादीनामादिलोपे। बहोरुत्तरेषामिष्ठेमेयसाम्। इष्ठेमेयःसु परतो बहोरिति सन्देहः। बहोरुत्तरेषामिष्ठेमेयसाम्। गोतो णित्। गोतः परस्य सर्वनामस्थानस्य सर्वनामस्थाने परतो गोत इति सन्देहः। गोतः परस्य सर्वनामस्थानस्य। रुदादिभ्यः सार्वधातुके। रुदादिभ्यः परस्य सार्वधातुकस्य। सार्वधातुके परतो रुदादीनामिति सन्देहः। रुदादिभ्यः परस्य सार्वधातुकस्य। आने मुगीदासः। आस उत्तरस्यानस्य। आने परत आस इति सन्देहः। आस उत्तरस्य आनस्य। आमि सर्वनाम्नः सुट्। सर्वनाम्न उत्तरस्यामः।
अथ यत्रोभयनिर्देशस्तत्र कस्य कार्येण भवितव्यम्? तत्र यानवकाशा सेतरस्याः षष्ठीं प्रकल्पयिष्यति, अतः षष्ठीनिर्दिष्टस्य कार्यं भविष्यति।

conditions.text: The rule does not apply where the sūtra decides the direction itself, or where the 5th has a different job. (a) An explicit पूर्व ('before'), प्राक्, or आङ् ('up to'): the operation is then on what precedes, or within a range. 7.3.44: 'पूर्वस्य किम्? परस्य मा भूत्'. (b) A 5th that is not dig-yoga: cause (hetu), distance (अदूरात्), a 5th governed by an unstated अन्य ('other than', 8.3.4), or 'what the suffix was enjoined after' (विहितस्य). Nyāsa (3.1.2) treats a 5th as dig-yoga only when no other reason for the 5th exists. (c) A word that only looks like a 5th: a substitute written with t (तात्, आत् = the substitute आ), or a 6th that the Kāśikā keeps as a 6th.

conditions.text: Limit (stated per sūtra): where a commentator says the त् of that sūtra is only for ease of pronunciation (मुखसुखार्थ / उच्चारणार्थ) — not for "that length only" — the tapara does no 1.1.70 work there; a stated denial is a ✖, not a ✔. Bālamanoramā (after the Śekhara) holds this generally for substitutes, against the Kāśikā's 6.4.41 example; this audit applies it only where it is said of the sūtra itself.

1.1.72 vt.2.gloss: …except an ugit or a SOUND as qualifier

conditions.text: Vārttika 1 on 1.1.72: in rules prescribing a samāsa or a pratyaya, tadanta-vidhi is barred (नडादिभ्यः फक् does not reach सूत्रनड). Vārttika 2: except where the qualifier is an ugit or a varṇa (sound). The Bhāṣya's examples: उगितश्च (भवती, अतिभवती) and अत इञ् (दाक्षिः).

quotes.quote: समासप्रत्ययविधौ प्रतिषेधः। समासविधौ प्रत्ययविधौ च प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः।
उगिद्वर्णग्रहणवर्जम्। उगिद्ग्रहणं वर्णग्रहणं च वर्जयित्वा। उगिद्ग्रहणमुगितश्च। भवती। अतिभवतौ।

conditions.text: What it requires: (1) a samāsa- or pratyaya-vidhi; (2) the base (prātipadika — or dhātu, see C3) is qualified by a sound or an ugit, so that "what ends in it" is read; (3) the sound is really a sound — not a homonymous dhātu/noun/saṃjñā, not a suffix name (that tadanta is PIS 23), not an उपधा or आदि qualifier, not a बह्वच्/द्व्यच् bahuvrīhi, and not already spelt out with अन्त in the sūtra.

quotes.quote: उगिद्वर्णेति । उगिता वर्णेन च प्रातिपदिकं विशेष्यमित्यर्थः ।

conditions.text: Scope caveat (dhātu suffix rules): the Śekhara restricts vt.1's pratyaya bar to sūtras that name a prātipadika by its form, and the Kāśikā gives एरच् and ओरावश्यके as plain 1.1.72 examples. On that reading vt.1 never arises in kṛt rules with a sound-qualified dhātu, so vt.2 is not strictly needed there. This audit follows the earlier 1.1.72 audit (vt.1 as the Bhāṣya states it is general to pratyaya-vidhi) and counts those credits licensed, flagged for Harsha.

1.1.72.generalExplanation: a qualifier (viśeṣaṇa), agreeing with the word it qualifies (viśeṣya), stands for whatever ENDS in it — so we read “…-अन्त”; only the qualifier, never the qualified word (Nyāsa: “विशेषणेन च तदन्तविधिः, न विशेष्येण”)

conditions.text: Definition: a word used as a viśeṣaṇa (qualifier) in a rule stands for whatever ENDS in it, and for itself.

quotes.quote: येन विशेषणेन विधिर्विधीयते स तदन्तस्यात्मान्तस्य समुदायस्य ग्राहको भवति, स्वस्य च रूपस्य।
विशेषणं तदन्तस्य संज्ञा स्यात् स्वस्य च रूपस्य ।

conditions.text: A viśeṣya must be present for the qualifier to qualify — by direct mention, by adhikāra, or by implication (sāmarthya/ākṣepa). With no viśeṣya (e.g. 6.1.78 एचोऽयवायावः, 6.1.87 आद्गुणः) tadanta-vidhi does not operate.

quotes.quote: विशेष्यसन्निधौ च विशेषणं भवति, सन्निधिश्च कुत्रचित्साक्षान्निर्देशेन, यथा-'ईदूदेद्द्विवचनम्' इति द्विवचनस्य । क्वचिदधिकारद्यथा-'एरच्' इति धातोः । क्वचिदाक्षेपाद्, यथा-'इको झल्' इति सना धातोः । 'एचोऽयवायावः' इत्यादौ न कथंचिद्विशेष्यसंनिधिरिति नैतत्प्रवर्तते ।
एवमपि'आद् गुणः' इत्यत्र आदित्यवर्णान्तो गृह्यते, अचीति चाजादेरिति खट्वेन्द्र इत्यादाववर्णान्तस्य समुदायस्याजादेश्च गुणप्रसङ्गः ।

conditions.text: Only the qualifier yields tadanta, never the qualified (viśeṣya) word itself; and a qualifier of the sound (grahaṇopādhi such as असंयोगपूर्व, ओष्ठ्यपूर्व) qualifies the sound, not the whole. So a sound that is the sthānin inside a suffix, a preceding member, or a meaning-qualifier does not produce "what ends in it".

quotes.quote: विशेषणेन चतदन्तविधिः, न विशेष्येण।
उकार एव विशेष्यते। उकारोयोऽसंयोगपूर्वस्तदन्तात् प्रत्ययादिति।

conditions.text: Vārttika 1 (1.1.72 vt.1): no tadanta in rules that prescribe a samāsa or a pratyaya when a specific word is named (नडादिभ्यः फक् does not apply to सूत्रनड; श्रितादिभिः not to परमश्रित). Vārttika 2: except ugit and varṇa (sound) qualifiers. The Śekhara restates the pratyaya part as "ग्रहणवता प्रातिपदिकेन तदन्तविधिर्नास्ति", limited to pratyaya-vidhi, with 5.2.87 सपूर्वाच्च as jñāpaka.

quotes.quote: समासप्रत्ययविधौ प्रतिषेधः। समासविधौ प्रत्ययविधौ च प्रतिषेधो वक्तव्यः।
प्रत्ययविधौ — <<नडादिभ्यः फक्>> [[४.१.९९]]। नडस्यापत्यं नाडायनः। इह मा भूत् — सूत्रनडस्यापत्यं सौत्रनाडिः।

conditions.text: Lifts of vt.1: (a) the strī-pratyaya section has tadanta-vidhi by jñāpaka (and "with the pradhāna"); (b) sāmūhika affixes have it by jñāpaka; (c) where the viśeṣya is itself a compound (bahuvrīhi, dvigu, tatpuruṣa, avyayībhāva, or a samāsānta rule) the named word must be its final member — tadanta by sāmarthya; (d) the Mahābhāṣya lists specific prayojanas (अपरिमाणबिस्त…, रथसीताहल…, सुसर्वार्धदिक्…, ऋतोर्वृद्धिमद्विधौ…, etc.); (e) an individual jñāpaka (4.1.139 कुलात्).

quotes.quote: एतदेव ज्ञापकम् — भवत्यस्मिन् प्रकरणे तदन्तविधिरिति।
अस्त्यत्र प्रकरणे तदन्तविधिरिति। तथा च प्रधानेन तदन्तविधिर्भवति।

quotes.quote: प्रत्ययग्रहणं च अपञ्चम्याः प्रयोजनम्। यञ्ञिञ्ञोः फग् भवति। गार्ग्यायणः। वात्स्यायनः। परमवात्स्यायनः।

conditions.text: A 7th-case sound qualifier naming the condition gives tadādi (what BEGINS with it) — PIS 33, an apavāda of tadanta.

quotes.quote: अल्ग्रहणेषु यस्मिन् विधिस्तदादाविति वक्तव्यम्।
तदन्तविधेरपवाद इयम् ।

conditions.text: Where the sūtra itself says "-अन्त" (or "उत्तरपद", "पदान्त"), no paribhāṣā is needed; the commentators treat the explicit anta as stated for some other purpose. Also a 5th-case sound may be read as tadanta when a viśeṣya is implied (6.1.69 एङन्तात्).

conditions.text: Definition and scope: in the (third) dhātu section, what is denoted by a 7th-case word of a sūtra is called upapada; the word expressing it (कुम्भ…) is the upapada, and the suffix comes only when it is present.

quotes.quote: तत्रैतस्मिन् धात्वधिकारे तृतीये यत् सप्तम्या निर्दिष्टं तदुपपदसंज्ञं भवति।
वाच्यत्वेन स्थितं कुम्भादि तद्वाचकं पदमुपपदसंज्ञं स्यात्तस्मिंश्च सत्येव वक्ष्यमाणः प्रत्ययः

conditions.text: Range: only the third dhātu-adhikāra, i.e. 3.1.91–3.4.117 (not e.g. च्लि लुङि 3.1.43).

conditions.text: Exclusion: a 7th-case word that states a MEANING (the suffix’s kāraka sense, a time, a circumstance) is not an upapada — by the commentators’ reading (व्याख्यानात्).

quotes.quote: 'धः कर्मणि ष्ट्रन्' 'भुवो भावे' इत्यादौ सप्तम्यन्तमर्थनिर्देशपरमेव, व्याख्यानादिति भाष्यकैयटादिषु स्पष्टम्

conditions.text: 3.1.94 is a paribhāṣā valid only inside the dhātu adhikāra (3.1.91–3.4.117): there an apavāda suffix that is NOT sarūpa with the utsarga blocks it only optionally, so the utsarga stays as an option. It does not reach beyond the heading.

conditions.text: The vārttika (read on 3.3.108) supplies two suffixes, इक् and श्तिप्, for CITING a dhātu by name: पचि / पचति (gen. पचेः / पचतेः).

quotes.quote: इक्श्तिपावित्येतौ प्रत्ययौ धातुनिर्देशे वक्तव्यौ। पचेर्ब्रूहि पचतेर्ब्रूहि।
इक्श्तिपौ धातुनिर्देशे॥ भिदिः। छिदिः। पचतिः। पठतिः॥

conditions.text: Citing (निर्देश) = repeating the root as a name (अनुकरण). The श्तिप् form carries the vikaraṇa and its substitutes (पचति with शप्; पिबति, जिघ्रति); the sūtras themselves use such forms (सुनोति, सुवति, स्यति, ध्यायतेः).

conditions.text: It is optional (बहुल): a root may also be cited bare (दृशः, यजः, खनः) — such a citation is NOT an instance of इक्/श्तिप्.

conditions.text: Not every final -इ on a root-name is इक्: an इ 'for pronunciation' on a substitute (वयि, गमि), an 'incidental' इ (इन्धि, कुण्डि), or the -इ of a ṇyanta stem (पूरि, एजि) are expressly distinguished from इक्.

4.1.82.gloss: a taddhita suffix comes after the first of the semantically connected words, in the case the sūtra names (samartha)
4.1.82.generalExplanation: a taddhita suffix goes after the first of the words able to take it, standing in the case the rule names

conditions.text: Scope. 4.1.82 is an adhikāra of three separate items — समर्थानाम्, प्रथमात्, वा — running from 4.1.83 up to (not including) 5.3.1 प्राग्दिशो विभक्तिः, i.e. through 5.2.140. It is not a vidhi of its own.

quotes.quote: त्रयमप्यधिक्रियते समर्थानामिति च, प्रथमादिति च, वेति च। स्वार्थिकप्रत्ययावधिश्चायमधिकारः, <<प्राग् दिशो विभक्तिः>>[[५.३.१]] इति यावत्।
विधेयस्याऽदर्शनान्नायं स्वतन्त्रविधिरिति मत्वाह — इदं पदत्रयमधिक्रियत इति ।

conditions.text: What it does. In the defining (lakṣaṇa) sentences of the section — तस्यापत्यम्, तेन रक्तं रागात्, तत्र भवः … — the suffix comes, optionally, after the FIRST-NAMED of the semantically connected words, i.e. the word standing in the case the sentence names (the samartha-vibhakti). Checkable predicate: the rule (or the lakṣaṇa-sentence it inherits) introduces a taddhita suffix, and the base of that suffix is the word in the named case.

quotes.quote: लक्षणवाक्यानि <<तस्यापत्यम्>> [[४.१.९२]] <<तेन रक्तं रागात्>> [[४.२.१]] <<तत्र भवः>> [[४.३.५३]] इत्येवमादीनि भविष्यन्ति। तेषु सामर्थ्ये सति प्रथमनिर्दिष्टादेव विकल्पेन प्रत्ययो भवतीति वेदितव्यम्।
समर्थानामिति निर्धारणे षष्ठी। समर्थानां मध्ये प्रथमः प्रत्ययप्रकृतित्वेन निर्धार्यते।

conditions.text: 'प्रथम' = first uttered in the rule's own sentence (the samartha-vibhakti word: तस्य, तेन, तत्र, सा/सः/तत्, तस्मै …), NOT the other words of that sentence. In particular the word naming the suffix's MEANING (अस्य, अस्मिन्, अस्मै, एषाम्, अनेन, इदम्, अपत्यम् …) is the pratyayārtha, not the samartha; and a word naming a suffix (यत्, इन, य …) is not a samartha word at all.

quotes.quote: प्रथमादिति किम्? षष्ठ्यन्ताद् यथा स्यात् प्रथमान्ताद् मा भूत्।
समर्थानां मध्ये प्रथमोच्चारितादित्यर्थः ।

conditions.text: 'वा' (the mahāvibhāṣā) makes every taddhita of the section optional against the plain sentence (vākya).

quotes.quote: वेति किम्? वाक्यमपि हि यथा स्यात् — उपगोरपत्यमिति।

conditions.text: Svārthika suffixes (the suffix adds no meaning beyond the base's own): समर्थ and प्रथम have nothing to work on (no second connected word), so only the वा part can apply — and even that is not uniform: some svārthikas are obligatory (Bhāṣya's list quoted by the Nyāsa).

quotes.quote: स्वार्थिकेषु ह्यस्योपयोगो नास्ति, विकल्पोऽपि तत्रानवस्थितः। केचिन्नित्यमेव भवन्ति।
तस्मात् समर्थतावा अभावात् स्वार्थिकेषु समर्थानामित्येतत् तावन्नोपयुज्यते। अत एव प्रतियोगिनोऽभावात् प्रथमादित्येतदपि नोपयुज्यत एव।

conditions.text: From 5.3.1 on, समर्थ and प्रथम stop; वा continues (making 5.3.x/5.4.x suffixes optional unless obligatory). So a credit after 5.2.140 is licensed only for the वा part.

quotes.quote: अतः परं स्वार्थिकाः प्रत्ययाः, तेषु समर्थाधिकारः प्रथमग्रहणं च प्रतियोग्यपेक्षत्वाद् नोपयुज्यत इति द्वयमपि निवृत्तम्। वावचनं तु वर्तत एव, तेन विकल्पेन तसिलादयो भवन्ति।
महाविभाषया चात्र प्रत्ययो विकल्प्यते।

conditions.text: (Derived from C2 — auditor's reading, stated so it can be challenged.) The rule places a suffix. At a rule whose OWN operation is a luk/lup of an already-introduced suffix, an āgama or ādeśa where the suffix is supplied by an earlier rule, a prohibition (न भवति), or no operation at all (a saṃjñā, a meaning-heading), 4.1.82 does nothing — unless a commentator reads it into that rule (C8). Kāśikā marks such rules explicitly.

quotes.quote: आदेशार्थं वचनम् प्रत्ययश्च पूर्वेणैव सिद्धः।
ततः पूर्वेणैवाण्प्रत्ययः सिद्धः, इकारादेशार्थं वचनम्।

conditions.text: A commentator may read part of 4.1.82 into a non-suffix rule inside the section; that is an application (licensed). Seen: Mahābhāṣya at 4.1.162 (प्रथम restricts the gotra-saṃjñā), Nyāsa at 4.1.88 (the वा makes the luk a vyavasthita-vibhāṣā). Merely NAMING 4.1.82 while discussing something else is not.

quotes.quote: न वक्तव्यम्। समर्थानां प्रथमाद्वा [[4.1.82]] इति वर्तते। समर्थानां प्रथमस्य यदपत्यं पौत्रप्रभृतीति विज्ञायते॥

conditions.text: A paribhāṣā on accent rules: wherever an udātta or svarita is taught, the pada is anudātta except the one vowel that rule gives its accent to.

quotes.quote: परिभाषेयं स्वरविधिविषया। यत्रान्यः स्वर उदात्तः स्वरितो वा विधीयते, तत्रानुदात्तं पदमेकं वर्जयित्वा भवतीत्येतदुपस्थितं द्रष्टव्यम्।
कः पुनरेको वर्ज्यते ? यस्यासौ स्वरो विधीयते।

conditions.text: It is kāryakāla: it is present at every rule where such an accent is taught, in the whole Saptādhyāyī (not only book 6) — so it is part of reading those rules.

quotes.quote: कार्यकालं संज्ञापरिभाषम् । यत्र कार्यं तत्रोपस्थितमिदं द्रष्टव्यम् ।
